title: Corporate Finance & Capital Structure Decision Making
description: Evaluate financing options (debt vs. equity), analyze capital structure costs, and make decisions for international expansion.

seo.overviewBody: Capital structure decisions determine how a business finances its growth through debt and equity. Corporate finance specialists prove competence by modeling WACC, evaluating financial leverage, analyzing debt covenant metrics, and assessing Modigliani-Miller capital trade-offs.

deliverables.title: 1. Capital Structure & WACC Optimization Model
deliverables.desc: Financial model (.xlsx) evaluating overall cost of capital across varying debt-to-equity ratio scenarios.

deliverables.title: 2. Debt Refinancing & Capital Cost Memo
deliverables.desc: Executive memo evaluating corporate bond issuance versus bank debt covenants and equity dilution.

deliverables.title: 3. Financial Leverage & Interest Coverage Report
deliverables.desc: Risk report analyzing Debt-to-EBITDA and Interest Coverage ratios under stress-tested EBITDA decline scenarios.

faqs.question: What is the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) formula for Cost of Equity?
faqs.answer: Cost of Equity (Ke) = Risk-Free Rate (Rf) + Beta * (Market Risk Premium).

faqs.question: What is the Trade-Off Theory of Capital Structure?
faqs.answer: Trade-off theory states that companies balance the tax benefit of debt (interest tax shields) against the increased costs of financial distress.

faqs.question: What is an Interest Coverage Ratio?
faqs.answer: Interest Coverage = EBIT / Interest Expense. Higher ratios indicate a safer buffer for servicing debt obligations.
